Interface ChaosEventListener

All Known Implementing Classes:
AsyncChaosEventListener, ChaosDecisionRecorder
Functional Interface:
This is a functional interface and can therefore be used as the assignment target for a lambda expression or method reference.
@FunctionalInterface public interface ChaosEventListener
Observer for all chaos lifecycle and effect-application events.

Register instances via ChaosControlPlane.addEventListener(ChaosEventListener).

Contract for implementations:

  • Non-blocking — listeners are invoked synchronously on the thread that triggers the chaos event. Any I/O, locking, or other blocking call inside onEvent adds latency to the instrumented JVM operation; wrap a slow listener with async(ChaosEventListener) to run it on an agent-owned thread.
  • Exceptions are contained — an exception thrown from onEvent is caught and logged (at WARNING the first time, then at FINE); it never reaches the application thread, and the other listeners still receive the event.
  • Shared events — every listener receives the same ChaosEvent instance (it is immutable; nothing is copied per listener).

Built-in listeners registered automatically:

  • A java.util.logging logger at INFO level (always active)
  • A JFR event bridge (registered automatically by the bootstrap module) when jdk.jfr is available at runtime

  • Method Details

    • onEvent

      void onEvent(ChaosEvent event)
      Called each time a chaos event occurs.
      Parameters:
      event - the immutable event; never null. Inspect ChaosEvent.type() to discriminate lifecycle events from application events.

    • async

      static ChaosEventListener async(ChaosEventListener delegate)
      Wraps delegate so that it receives events on an agent-owned thread instead of the thread that triggered them: the control plane queues each event (a bounded queue; events beyond its capacity are dropped and counted in the diagnostics' droppedEvents) and returns immediately. Use it for listeners that log, export or block, so their latency never reaches an intercepted application call. Events are delivered in order. The thread has no context class loader, so it keeps no class loader of the thread that registered the listener reachable.
      Parameters:
      delegate - the listener to call off the triggering thread
      Returns:
      a listener to register with ChaosControlPlane.addEventListener(ChaosEventListener)
